body:
Today's scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities across either platform — a quiet day, and worth taking at face value rather than reading into it. Gold itself is trading in the mid-$4,400s as of the most recent session, down about 1.95% versus the prior day, at $4441.10, a level consistent with where the Kalshi and Polymarket strike ladders are clustered.

Both books are pricing that spot level sensibly. On Kalshi, the September 30, 2026 settle above ladder crosses 50/50 right around the $4,410 strike (bid 0.53, ask 0.56), which lines up with gold trading in the $4,400s right now — exactly what you'd expect from an efficient settlement market with the underlying already near that threshold. The year-end $4,300 or above contract sits at 0.71/0.72, implying the market sees it as fairly likely gold holds above that level through December, which is unsurprising given gold has been in a strong uptrend, recently closing at $4,539.90, its best day in weeks, after comments from a Fed governor.

The one thing worth flagging for readers, not as an opportunity but as a caution: several Polymarket weekly touch contracts (e.g., the week-of-September-7 $4,300 and $4,400 low-touch markets) show bid-ask spreads as wide as 0.01 to 0.97-0.99. That is not a mispriced market waiting to be arbed — it is simply an illiquid, thin order book with almost no resting size on one side, common in short-dated weekly contracts with low volume. Touch contracts also resolve on intraday high/low prints rather than a single settlement value, so they aren't directly comparable to Kalshi's settle-style contracts even when the strike price matches, which is why the scanner correctly excluded them from today's opportunity list.
headline: No arbitrage found as gold settles near $4,441; wide Polymarket spreads reflect illiquidity, not mispricing
